deep.body: After RENDER press Show my files on the green Saved bar. Then press Ctrl+R in iRacing with your car on track. If the car changes, it was a reload problem; if not, go back to the cause list.

articles.title: The car looks smeared or blobby
articles.summary: Blobby appearance needs source, detail, mask and preview diagnosis. Texture scale, selection feather, source pixel quality and paint-value blending are separate; a file format or0.5scale does not guarantee sharp calibrated features.
articles.what: First distinguish source-art softness, generated base detail, paint-pattern placement, selection feather and reduced preview coverage. Base Scale is only one contributor. Changing every scale together can hide the actual cause and alter a correct material. Scale controls operate on particular contributors and coordinate paths; exact visual feature size is not a universal promise across finishes or car templates. Identify the base/pattern/spec contributor, compare its actual result and retain fine detail rather than treating0.5 as a calibrated car-space ruler. Spec Scale follows the linked base placement unless Independent Spec is enabled, while explicit colour placement can also use Colour Scale. Inspect linked/independent settings and the relevant contributor before diagnosing a paint-versus-spec size difference as blurry source art. Inspect the actual pixel dimensions and visible source detail. A container or extension does not prove that previously softened artwork has regained detail. A large file with blurred source pixels can still look soft; preserve the best original artwork rather than repeatedly converting formats. The reviewed source-layer normalization resizes mismatched masks with INTER_AREA, then thresholds ownership at0.5. Fine edge occupancy can differ at reduced resolution. Compare intended full-size coverage before enlarging the finish primitives or assuming the texture source is corrupt. Selection feather is a separate mask operation. The layer RGB colour fast path feathers its colour-union mask after matching. Texture scale does not repair that selection boundary; inspect the intended coverage and feather setting independently. Matching identical RGB does not supply spatial separation. Use inspected layer ownership or a checked spatial mask to protect shared-colour artwork. Tighter tolerance alone is not a substitute for choosing which pixels belong to the number or body. The actual Blend compositor keeps source hue/saturation and uses normalized pattern luminance to change value. A softer-looking result can therefore be a paint-value treatment rather than lost source resolution. Compare source, composed paint and mask before resizing or replacing the source.

articles.title: The app will not start or update
articles.summary: If Shokker shows Server Failed, the paint engine could not start: the usual causes are antivirus software blocking it, a missing Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable, or another program using its port. Updates install from the banner and need a full restart.
articles.what: SYMPTOM: Shokker Paint Booth opens to an error box, a blank window, or an old screen after an update. CAUSE: the window and the paint engine are two parts. If the engine does not start within about a minute, Shokker shows a Server Failed box that lists the common causes and the name of its debug log. After an update the window can briefly be newer or older than the engine.
when: A box titled Server Failed appears when you open Shokker.
The window is blank or stuck on loading.
After an update the app acts strangely or shows a version warning.
The Download Update banner will not go away.
how: Read the actual startup dialog. Server Failed names the debug log and lists possible paint-engine startup causes; those possibilities are not a diagnosis of your PC.

If another Shokker copy is running, close that duplicate and try starting the intended app. For a missing Visual C++ runtime or a security block, use the specific error/log to identify the required repair; do not disable protection indiscriminately.
Keep the named debug log and use Report a Problem if the window opens, or provide it to Shokker support when startup continues to fail.
For an update problem, record the installed version and download/install error. Save work before any requested restart; this answer does not install an update or restart the app.

articles.title: Error messages explained
articles.summary: Most red messages in Shokker have one plain cause and one fix. Paste the exact message into the chat and the helper explains it, or find it in this list. A present-but-invalid source-layer restriction produces empty coverage in the inspected engine helper; increasing finish strength will not repair malformed mask data. Keep the protection and re-establish the restriction, using the exact warning for diagnosis.
articles.what: Shokker's error messages come from the render, the preview, the car folder and the paint engine. The Chat helper recognises each of them when you paste the text, and the Check my setup button reads your live settings instead of guessing. Each line below is: the message, what it means, and what to do.
when: A red banner or toast appeared.
You want to know what a message means before you try fixes.
how: Copy the exact message text (or take a screenshot).
Paste it into the Chat panel: the helper matches it to the list and answers in plain words.
Or find it below, do the fix, and render again.
If nothing matches, press Check my setup, then Settings gear > Report a Problem and send the report to Shokker support.
tips: A render is already running / render_busy: only one render at a time. Wait about a minute, then press RENDER again. If it never clears, close and reopen Shokker.

OPEN PAINT FIRST / LOADING PAINT / Set the Source Paint path / Source Paint needs a FULL path: open your car template with Open Paint... (Layered template or Flat image), wait until loading ends, or paste the full path, not just a file name.
Enter your iRacing User ID (4-7 digits): type your Customer ID (helmet icon > Profile in iRacing). It is not your car number.
To render: pick a color on the paint (Pick + Add), then assign a Finish: every zone needs a colour AND a finish. Muted zones are skipped. Also shown as No valid zones.

Paint engine is offline / Render server unreachable / engine hung: the engine restarts itself. Wait 10 seconds. If it stays down, close Shokker completely and reopen it; antivirus can block the engine.
Timed out after 5 minutes: the design is too heavy. Use fewer zones or simpler stacks.
aggregate RLE decode budget exceeded / decode failed / out of memory / too many zones: more than about 20 zones with their own painted area. Undo, merge zones, or say start over.
OUTPUT FOLDER ERROR / iRacing output folder not found / No active car configured / No iRacing folder set: the iRacing Car Folder is empty or wrong. Pick the car's folder with the car menu.
Failed to push / PermissionError / Copy verification failed: another program holds the file. Close the iRacing paint preview or 3D Car Viewer and any image viewer, then render again.
Unknown base / pattern id ... Did you mean: a zone uses a finish that was retired or renamed. Open that zone, pick another finish, render again.
Finish Pack needed: the finish lives in a downloadable pack that is not installed. Install it from the Finish Packs screen if your version has one, then restart, or pick another finish.
cross_origin_forbidden: you opened Shokker in a browser tab by hand. Use the Shokker Paint Booth window.
Job not found / Deploy to a different car: Shokker keeps only the two newest renders. Render again, then press Deploy Now.
iRacing TGA must be 2048 / strict 2048: this step needs an exact 2048 by 2048 paint. Open the car's own template at its normal size; do not resize the canvas.
Preview failed - showing the LAST GOOD render: press F5. If it repeats, undo the last change or merge zones.
Source layer is missing / restricted layer / painting nothing: the zone is limited to a hidden or missing layer. Show the layer or clear Restrict to layer.
Heads up: app v... vs ui v...: the screen is older or newer than the engine. Close and reopen Shokker fully.
Autosave is off for this design: the design is too big for automatic save. Save an SPB project now.
pitfalls: A message can be a warning, not an error: yellow notes about PSD blend modes or layers are information.
Messages that mention a port, a path or a log mean the app wrote more detail to its debug log.

articles.title: PSD will not open or has wrong layers
articles.summary: Read the import error and completion diagnostics; a fixed wait or a displayed composite is not proof of complete editable import.
articles.what: SYMPTOM: the template will not open, loads slowly, or some layers are missing, flat or look different. CAUSE: the layered import reads Photoshop, GIMP and OpenRaster files and rebuilds each pixel layer. Layers that are not plain pixels (text, shapes, adjustment layers) cannot be imported, some blend modes are turned into Normal, and unusual group settings make Shokker open the flattened picture instead. A failed import leaves your previous paint unchanged.

how: Use Open Paint... > PSD/XCF/ORA or Open Layered for a layered template. Read the exact error or completion note before retrying; do not treat a one-minute wait as proof of success.

Check whether the layer list and note report decoded pixels, missing non-pixel layers, unsupported blend normalization, or a source-composite fallback. A displayed picture does not prove every layer imported as editable artwork.
Preserve the original template. If a layer lacks pixels or an unsupported blend is reported, prepare a compatible copy in your editor and inspect the new import; do not overwrite the only original.
An import error retains the previous source in the guarded workflow. Check the current Source Paint and actual layer list before making edits or retrying.

articles.title: Everything looks tiny or huge (base scale)
articles.summary: Separate finish detail, source artwork size and editor zoom. Base Scale and Spec Scale are linked unless Independent Spec is enabled; colour scale can multiply Base Scale in the explicit colour path. There is no universal texture-size guarantee for every template.
articles.what: When a woven check, groove, flake or other finish detail seems too large or small, first identify which contributor supplies it. BASE SCALE places generated base detail; SPEC SCALE follows it by default, or can be independent. The active link normalizes these scales to 0.05–5.00 in 0.05 steps. In the reviewed explicit base-colour path, Base Scale multiplies Colour Scale. Editor zoom changes the view, while artwork resizing changes image pixels; neither establishes a calibrated physical feature size on a car. Source-passing bases must not tile the source livery because Base Scale was reduced. Constant plain materials contain no generated grain to resize.
when: A texture is far too big or small for the look you want.
You changed Base Scale and the colours did not change.
Spec and paint no longer line up.
how: Identify whether the unwanted size belongs to the base paint, base material texture, pattern, additional-base coverage or original artwork.
For generated base detail, inspect Base Scale. To change only material placement, enable Independent Spec and inspect Spec Scale.
Check Colour Scale too when using the explicit base-colour path: 0.50 Base Scale times 0.50 Colour Scale means 0.25 effective colour scale there.
If the artwork itself is the wrong size, use the appropriate image/layer sizing workflow; if only the view is wrong, adjust editor zoom.
Compare the selected finish in the actual target and template. Do not enlarge every primitive merely because the fit view hides fine detail.

faq.q: Does Base Scale always leave colours unchanged?
faq.a: No universal claim applies. A source-passing base should retain the imported artwork, but a generated palette can move or repeat differently when its placement changes. The explicit colour path also multiplies Base Scale by Colour Scale.

faq.q: Why is my whole car small in the window?
faq.a: If only the view is small, adjust editor zoom. Finish scale changes generated detail; it does not resize the car artwork.

faq.q: Are red gingham squares a fixed size after I resize the template?
faq.a: No. The registered Red Gingham source uses 12-pixel colour bands in a 24-pixel coordinate repeat, but finish placement, resizing and template mapping affect the displayed result. A source repeat is not a guaranteed physical check size on the car.

faq.q: How do I resize the shine texture without moving my painted design?
faq.a: Enable Independent Spec for the selected zone and change Spec Scale. Confirm that the chosen material actually has spatial detail; a constant plain material has no grain to resize. Check other paint contributors separately.

faq.q: Do all scale controls work independently?
faq.a: No. Base Scale and Spec Scale are linked by default. The explicit base-colour path multiplies Base Scale and Colour Scale; additional-base scatter size controls coverage rather than necessarily resizing its material texture.

faq.q: Is 0.5 the best scale for every finish?
faq.a: No. Choose the intended detail size for that finish and target, inspect actual output and keep artwork readability in mind. A universal numerical recommendation is not supported.

faq.q: My finish grain is too coarse but the shine is right; which control should I change first?
faq.a: Texture scale and contribution strength solve different problems. Adjust sampled structure rather than using strength as a size control. More strength changes contribution, not primitive dimensions.

articles.title: Opening TGA files in other editors, blurry logos and getting a PNG
articles.summary: Shokker writes plain TGA files (the paint is 24-bit; the spec is 32-bit, because its alpha is the lighting mask); Export to Photoshop, Export PNG (canvas right-click) and Channel PNG Export get them into other tools. A blurry logo is almost always a small picture that was enlarged.
articles.what: The paint and spec files are plain, uncompressed TGA pictures at the size of the template you opened (2048 x 2048, or 1024 x 1024): the paint is 24-bit, and the spec is 32-bit because its alpha channel carries the lighting mask. Any picture editor that reads TGA can open them. For a round trip through Photoshop, the layer Actions menu has Export to Photoshop, which writes named TGA exchange files plus a manifest so the edited files come back in. Shokker has no TGA-to-PNG converter as such, but two exports give you PNG files: Export PNG on the canvas right-click menu downloads a PNG of the current paint, and Channel PNG Export (PNG Channels Export under MORE TOOLS in the ZONES column) writes paint_base.png, spec_full.png and the separated spec channels for inspection. Logos look blurry when a small picture is stretched over a big area of the 2048 x 2048 sheet; start from a bigger picture rather than enlarging it with Transform.
when: Your editor will not open a TGA from Shokker.
You need a PNG of the paint or spec.
A logo or number looks soft or blurry on the car.
how: 1. To edit outside Shokker: layer Actions menu > Export to Photoshop, pick the car file name and an export folder, edit, then bring the files back.
2. For a PNG of what you see: right-click the canvas and choose Export PNG.

3. For the spec as PNGs: use PNG Channels Export (ZONES column > MORE TOOLS) or Channel PNG Export (in the SHOKK file library, for a saved SHOKK file), with an export folder; it writes paint_base.png, spec_full.png and one picture per channel.
4. For a sharp logo: add it with Actions > Place image... from a large PNG with a transparent background, then shrink it into place with Transform (Ctrl+T) instead of enlarging a small one.
5. Re-render and reload in iRacing (Ctrl+R) to see the sharp version.
tips: Channel PNG Export is for looking at the files; it does not make the final iRacing TGA. Render does that.
pitfalls: A paint TGA saved with the template's alpha channel can make parts of the car vanish or turn black in iRacing; keep the paint 24-bit (cars with paintable glass are the exception and need the glass alpha). The spec map is meant to carry alpha.
Enlarging a logo with Transform cannot add detail; it only spreads the pixels further.

articles.title: Frame rate: does a custom paint slow iRacing down?
articles.summary: Shokker cannot measure or change your frame rate in iRacing; it only writes files. Every render is the template's size (2048 or 1024 square) whatever finish you pick, so a busy finish does not make the paint bigger.
articles.what: Shokker runs outside iRacing and writes a paint and a spec map into the car folder. Their size is not a setting: it is the size of the template you opened, and iRacing paints are 2048 by 2048 or 1024 by 1024. A plain colour and the busiest finish give files of the same size in pixels. How iRacing handles custom paints is set in iRacing's own graphics options, for example its 2048 paint textures option, which needs an iRacing restart after you change it. Inside Shokker, what costs time is the render: more zones, big masks and heavy finishes take longer.
when: You worry that a detailed paint costs frames in iRacing.
Your league asks about texture size.
Shokker itself feels slow while rendering.
how: 1. Keep the template size: never resize the canvas; Shokker renders at the size of the template you opened.
2. For iRacing performance, use iRacing's graphics options; after changing the 2048 paint textures option, restart iRacing.
3. If renders in Shokker are slow, merge zones that share one look and keep heavy finishes to the areas that need them.
4. If a render keeps running for minutes, follow the render slow or failing article.
tips: Detail costs render time in Shokker, not pixels in the file: the file is the same size either way.
pitfalls: Resizing the paint to save memory breaks it: iRacing ignores sizes other than 2048 or 1024 square.
Shokker cannot show your frame rate; check it in iRacing.

articles.title: My car looks like plastic, fake or like a toy
articles.summary: A flat, plastic or unexpected shine needs a diagnosis: check spec delivery, intended body or logo target, material channels and strength. Zero metallic is valid for plain glossy paint; adding metal everywhere is not a universal fix.
articles.what: Source paint and material appearance are different things. Use source paint skips the ordinary primary base paint function, but the chosen material still supplies spec. Preserved artwork can therefore look different under reflections and lighting without its source RGB being repainted. Check other paint contributors separately: patterns, additional-base paint and colour adjustments can still alter the composed artwork. Plain Foundation Gloss starts at M/R/CC 0/30/16, while Matte starts at 0/200/160 in the merged registry: both have zero metal but different roughness and clearcoat. Uniform gloss can be an intentional design choice. These registered starting values do not certify a particular simulator appearance or the final composed pixels.
when: Your car looks like plastic or a toy in iRacing.
The paint looks fake or cheap next to other cars.
The colours are right but the car has no depth.
how: Identify the symptom and location: unchanged artwork but different reflections, an unexpectedly matte body, altered sponsor shine, or no visible spec effect in iRacing.
For a delivery problem, follow the export and iRacing troubleshooting guide. Inspect the existing output filename and destination; do not change material settings just to diagnose a missing file.

For a material problem, inspect the intended zone or layer target, the combined spec and its R METAL, G ROUGH and B COAT channels. Black in R METAL means nonmetal; it does not prove that gloss is broken.
To keep existing artwork during an ordinary primary-base material change, choose BASE COLOR Use source paint (spec only). Check patterns, additional-base paint and adjustments separately.
Check Spec Strength and overlay coverage. Strength moves the ordinary base toward M/R/CC 0/128/16; reducing it is not guaranteed to soften reflections and may make a matte base smoother.

Choose metal, satin, gloss or matte according to the intended surface and protect sponsor and number material separately. Compare one deliberate change at a time in the actual intended viewing conditions.
tips: Ask which surface should change before recommending a finish.
Keep number and sponsor readability in mind when considering texture; a plain surface is a valid choice.
A spec preview helps inspect channels; it is not acceptance of the final in-simulator reflections.
pitfalls: Do not diagnose M = 0 as a fault: plain Foundation Gloss is nonmetal.
Do not repaint source artwork solely because its material appearance changed.
Do not assume source-paint mode also protects logo material or disables additional-base paint.
Do not promise that adding metallic, lowering strength or adding texture will fix every flat-looking result.

deep.heading: Why an even shine reads as plastic
deep.body: Real car paint is colour over metal flake under a clear coat, and the light changes a little from spot to spot. Metal 0 with the same roughness and coat everywhere has none of that, which is what moulded plastic looks like. A little metal, a fine flake and a change of surface between neighbours give the eye the cues of real paint.

deep.body: Sparkle and depth depend on the sun and the angle, so judge them in the sim. Shokker writes the shine to car_spec_<ID>.tga; if that file is not in the car folder, or iRacing was not reloaded with Ctrl+R, the car keeps the old shine.

faq.q: Why does the metallic paint look different even if the artwork colour did not change?

faq.q: Does zero metallic mean my glossy paint is broken?
faq.a: No. Plain Foundation Gloss starts at M/R/CC 0/30/16 in the merged registry. Zero metal is valid for a nonmetal surface. Inspect roughness, clearcoat, strength, target and spec delivery rather than adding metal automatically.

faq.q: My car looks like plastic. Should I add metal everywhere?
faq.a: No universal setting fixes that symptom. First distinguish a missing spec file from an unsuitable material or wrong target. Zero metal can be deliberate glossy paint. Choose material for the body separately from sponsors and numbers; uniform gloss is also a valid design choice.

faq.q: How do I tell a missing spec file from an unsuitable material?
faq.a: First verify the existing spec output filename and destination using the export and iRacing troubleshooting guide. If delivery is correct, inspect the intended target and combined spec channels, strength and overlays. Changing metal values will not repair a file that never reached the simulator.

articles.title: Shokker closed or crashed: will I lose my layers?
articles.summary: Shokker saves your layers as you work. After a crash or a power cut, open the same file again and a message offers to restore your added layers, live text, painted layers, masks and adjustment layers.
articles.what: While you work, Shokker keeps a recovery copy of the layers you added, the layers you painted on, your live text, layer masks and adjustment layers, with their order, visibility, opacity and blend modes. If the app closed unexpectedly, open the same file again (Open Paint... > Layered template, or Flat image for a TGA, PNG or JPEG; it may reopen by itself). A message starts "SPB found your work from an interrupted session for this exact source" and lists what comes back, for example "2 added layers (1 live text layer) and 1 painted layer come back with their pixels", "2 layer masks also come back" and "1 adjustment layer also comes back with its settings". Click to restore. The whole restore is one undo step. If some layers had not been saved yet, the message says they will come back empty. A flat image (TGA, PNG or JPEG) works too: the layers you added on top of it come back when you open that same file again. The restore also brings back the car tools: Car-Space Fade, Sponsor Kit, Number Kit, Race Wear, Layer Materials (with Auto Spec results), Colourway variants, Car Stripe layers, brushed materials and the Edge Bleed setting. One Ctrl+Z undoes the whole restore and Ctrl+Y brings it back.
when: Shokker closed, froze or crashed while you were working.
The power went off or the computer restarted.
You closed the window by accident without saving.
how: 1. Start Shokker again and open the same file (Open Paint... > Layered template, or Flat image). It may reopen by itself.
2. Read the message that starts "SPB found your work from an interrupted session". It lists the layers, masks and adjustment layers that can come back.
3. Choose to restore. Your layers return with their pixels, order, opacity and visibility.
4. Check the layers, then save a project right away (Save / Open) so you have a proper file.
5. Render again if you need new paint files for iRacing.
tips: iRacing tip: recovery brings back your work in Shokker. The paint files that iRacing reads are only updated when you press RENDER, so render again and press Ctrl+R in iRacing.
Recovery is a safety net, not a save. Save a project at the end of every stretch of work.
It matches the exact source file, so use the same template you were working on.
pitfalls: Recovery needs the exact same file: reopen the same layered template, or the same TGA, PNG or JPEG you were working on.
If you open a different file, the recovery copy is not offered, and the app says so.

deep.heading: What comes back
deep.body: Layers you added (blank layers, live text, images), layers from your template that you painted on, and your layer order, names, opacity, blend modes, visibility, locks, clipping and effects. Live text is still live text after the restore. Layer masks and adjustment layers come back too, adjustment layers with their settings.

deep.heading: What it does not cover
deep.body: It restores the layers of a layered template (PSD, XCF or ORA) and the layers you added on top of a flat image (TGA, PNG or JPEG) when you reopen that same file. It also does not replace a saved project: if you open a different file, nothing is offered. Save a project at the end of each stretch of work.

deep.heading: It is one undo step
deep.body: Restoring is a single step in the undo list. If you restore and then change your mind, press Ctrl+Z once to go back to how the file looked before the restore.

faq.q: Does Shokker save my layers by itself?
faq.a: It keeps a recovery copy while you work and offers it back after a crash. It is not the same as saving a project, so save one yourself too.

faq.q: Do I get my live text back?
faq.a: Yes. Live text layers come back as live text, so you can still edit the words.

faq.q: Do masks and adjustment layers come back?
faq.a: Yes. The message says how many layer masks and adjustment layers come back.

faq.q: It did not offer to restore anything.
faq.a: You opened a different file. Open the same layered template or flat image you were using.

faq.q: Can I undo the restore?
faq.a: Yes. It is a single undo step. Press Ctrl+Z once.

faq.q: Does a crash restore bring back Race Wear, Sponsor Kit, Number Kit and Car-Space Fade?
faq.a: Yes. They come back with the rest of your layers. Open the same file again and choose to restore.

mistakes.cause: They had not been saved yet when the app closed.
mistakes.fix: Redo those layers and save a project.

protips: After a restore, save a project straight away. A saved project keeps every layer, mask, adjustment layer and live text.

articles.title: My number or lettering is cut off at the edge of a panel
articles.summary: Anything outside the paintable area of a panel is thrown away, so a number or lettering that hangs over a panel edge or a seam gets chopped there. Move it fully inside the panel, or make it smaller.
articles.what: The paint is one flat sheet of the car cut open. The Mask layer marks which part is a panel (paintable) and which is dead space between the panels. Artwork that runs past the edge of a panel into dead space is thrown away, and a number or word that crosses from one panel to the next is split where the sheet is cut, so it looks chopped on the car. Fix it by moving or shrinking the artwork so it sits fully inside one panel with a small gap to the edge.
when: The last digit of a number is missing at the edge of a door or quarter panel.
Lettering is cut in half where two panels meet.
A logo or number hangs over the edge of the hood, roof or trunk in the Car view.
how: 1. Turn on the Wire view (the outline of each panel) and the Mask view (what is paintable), so you can see the panel edge.
2. In LAYER mode pick Move (V) and click the number or lettering. Smart guides help you line it up.
3. Drag it fully inside the panel, or press Ctrl+T (Transform) and make it a little smaller.
4. Leave a small gap between the artwork and the panel edge.
5. Render and look at the Car view. The flat sheet can hide an edge problem that the car shows.
tips: iRacing tip: a number that runs onto the next panel is split in the sim. Put one number on each side panel instead of one big number across both.
If iRacing stamps the car number for you, keep its reserved block clear (see Safe areas).
Bold, simple numbers need less room at the edge than thin ones, so they survive a small mistake better.
pitfalls: Do not stretch a number to fill the panel: it will reach the edge again.
If the whole number is gone or changed colour, this is not the problem; a zone painted over it (see Numbers or sponsors vanished).

deep.heading: Why the edge chops it
deep.body: Only the panels of the car are paintable. The space between them is dead space, and paint there never reaches the car. A number that overhangs a panel is cut at the edge of the Mask. A number that crosses from one panel to the next is cut where the flat sheet is cut open, so the two halves do not meet on the car.

deep.heading: How to see the edge
deep.body: In the layer list turn on Wire (green outlines around each panel) and Mask (paintable areas). They are guide layers: RENDER leaves them out of the car paint for you. Move the number until it sits fully inside the outline, then check the Car view after a render.

deep.heading: When the number is stamped for you
deep.body: Some cars get a number stamped by iRacing in a reserved block. Keep that block clear if you want the sim to place it. If the number is part of your paint, choose Custom Number in the Car group.

faq.q: Why is the last digit of my number missing?

faq.q: Can one number go across two panels?

faq.q: How do I see where the panel edge is?
faq.a: Turn on the Wire view for panel outlines and the Mask view for the paintable area, in the layer list.

faq.a: No. If the whole number vanished or changed colour, a zone painted over it. See Numbers or sponsors vanished.

articles.title: A gradient looks banded or stepped in iRacing
articles.summary: Banding is the stair-step look of a long, smooth fade: each colour channel has only 256 levels and iRacing squeezes the texture, so a gentle ramp splits into visible bands. Fix it with the dither in the Gradient tool Colours ramp, more colour stops, a stronger or shorter fade, or a finish with fine texture over it.
articles.what: A paint file stores each of red, green and blue in 8 bits, which is 256 levels. A fade from one dark colour to a slightly lighter dark colour across the whole 2048-pixel sheet only passes through a few of those levels, and every level becomes one wide stripe, so twenty levels over 2000 pixels is a band about 100 pixels wide. Shokker hides this on screen because the preview is smaller and softer. Then iRacing makes it worse: it squeezes the paint into a compressed game texture that keeps fewer colours per small block, and it builds smaller copies of the texture (mips) that it shows at distance, so the steps stand out on the car. The longer and gentler the ramp, the wider each band. Dark, low-contrast fades band the most. Shokker has four ways to fight it. The Gradient tool Colours ramp adds a touch of dither, noise of about half a colour step, that breaks up the stair-steps. More colour stops, or a bigger colour difference, make more levels change over the same distance. A shorter fade makes each band narrower. And a finish with micro-texture (flake, pearl or fine grain) on the same zone hides the band edges under tiny speckle.
when: A gradient looks banded, stepped or striped in iRacing but smooth in Shokker.
A long dark fade shows contour lines on the car.
You want to dither a gradient or add noise so it does not band.
how: 1. Use the Colours ramp. In LAYER mode pick the Gradient tool (G), click Colours next to Linear and Reverse, pick a preset chip or click the colour bar to add a stop, then drag the fade. The ramp made by the editor carries the dither; a plain two-colour drag without Colours does not.

2. Add colour stops. Click the colour bar to add an in-between colour that shifts hue a little, so red, green and blue step at different places and the bands blend. A zone BASE COLOR set to Custom gradient takes 2 to 10 stops.
3. Push the colours further apart, or shorten the fade, so it passes through more levels over less distance.
4. Put a finish with micro-texture on the same zone, such as a flake or pearl finish or a fine-grain finish from the Surface Grain shelf; the speckle hides the band edges.
5. Judge it in the sim, not the preview: RENDER, press Ctrl+R in iRacing and look at the car from the distance you race at.
tips: RENDER already adds dither to the spec map when it writes it, so a smooth shine fade is covered; the paint fade is the one to dither.
Shokker has no Add Noise filter menu: the Colours ramp dither and a textured finish are the tools.
pitfalls: A dark, gentle fade across the whole sheet bands more than a bright, short one.
Two neighbouring stops of nearly the same colour add nothing; give each stop a clearly different colour.

deep.heading: Why 8 bits band
deep.body: Each colour channel has 256 levels. A fade that only moves the colour by 20 levels over the whole sheet has 20 stripes however smooth the maths, and the eye picks out stripe edges on a smooth dark surface much more easily than on a busy one.

deep.heading: Why it shows in iRacing and not in Shokker
deep.body: The Shokker preview is smaller and softer, so the stripes are hidden. iRacing loads the paint as a compressed texture, where small blocks of pixels share a reduced palette, and shows smaller mip copies at distance. Both turn gentle ramps into visible steps.

deep.heading: What the Colours ramp does for you
deep.body: When the Gradient tool paints a ramp made in the Colours editor, it adds one level of fixed noise (plus or minus half a colour step) to every pixel. That noise lets neighbouring pixels land on different levels, so the hard stripe edge becomes a fine grain that the eye reads as a smooth fade.

faq.q: Why does my gradient look banded in iRacing but smooth in Shokker?
faq.a: Colour has only 256 levels per channel, the preview hides the steps, and iRacing compresses the texture and shows mips at distance. A long gentle ramp turns into visible stripes.

faq.q: How do I stop gradient banding?
faq.a: Make the fade with the Gradient tool Colours ramp (it adds dither), add colour stops, push the colours further apart, or put a flake, pearl or fine-grain finish on the same zone.

faq.q: Does Shokker dither gradients?
faq.a: The Gradient tool Colours ramp does, and RENDER dithers the spec map. A plain two-colour gradient without Colours has no dither.

faq.q: Can I add noise to a gradient so it does not band?
faq.a: There is no Add Noise filter. Use the Colours ramp dither, or a finish with micro-texture on the zone.

faq.q: Which gradients band the most?
faq.a: Long, gentle, dark and low-contrast fades, because they cover the fewest colour levels over the most distance.

faq.q: Does a zone gradient band too?
faq.a: It can. Give BASE COLOR, Custom gradient more stops and clearer colour differences, and add a finish with fine texture.

faq.q: What makes the banding and chromosome ends respond differently in Chromosome Riot?
faq.a: On-shape metallic depends on tiers and the banding field; clearcoat follows a different banding formula. Telomere masks set high metallic and low roughness before enrichment. Look for banding-versus-end contrast when comparing it with cell-based motifs. No biological accuracy or real fluorescence is implied. These are source formulas before enrichment, clipping and engine composition, not exact final pixel readings. Metallic, roughness and clearcoat are material channels, not paint colours or physical percentages.

mistakes.fix: Use the Colours ramp (dither), add an in-between stop or a bigger colour difference, then RENDER and reload in iRacing.
